title: Personal assistant — hybrid architecture
summary: A chat assistant. Code owns the loop, budgets, and the effect gate. Claude plans and proposes tool calls. MCP is the tool standard. Composio covers the long tail. Send, delete, and pay wait for an exact approval.
autonomy: Hybrid, bounded agent with approvals (Ch1, Ch24). The model chooses the next tool inside a step budget. Code chooses the model, the allowlist, whether a call may run, and when to stop. External effects always wait for the owner.

layers.name: Users and channels
layers.boundary_below: session auth and a typed body

key_decisions: Hybrid: the model proposes tools, code allowlists and gates them (Ch24, Ch48)
Send, delete, and pay always wait for an exact, single-use approval (Ch49)
One research sub-agent, read-only, one hop. No crew (Ch31)
MCP hub plus Composio. Own OAuth for Gmail is an extension (Ch28, Ch29)
Tool results and events are data, never instructions (Ch47)
Release only when the golden gate says PROMOTE (Ch45)
rationale: Bounded agent, not a fixed procedure: a personal chat does not know the steps in advance, so the path has to depend on observations. Budgets, the allowlist, and the effect gate stay in code (Ch24, Ch13).
Plan-execute on top of ReAct: the planner's JSON is validated before tools run. The loop inside a step is ReAct with a step budget (Ch13).
One specialist: research gets its own context and a read-only tool list. Email and coding specialists are the same port, not enabled, because a second writer is not justified yet (Ch31).
Tools: one result envelope, dynamic selection, fail closed. MCP does not authorize. The host does (Ch11, Ch29).
Memory is separate from checkpoints and from the effect ledger. Facts are owner-scoped and cannot change the gate (Ch18, Ch19).
Postgres is the durable queue and the vector store for v1. Redis, pgvector, and S3 are extension points behind the same interfaces (Ch51).
trust_boundaries: Browser to gateway: better-auth session, size limit, jailbreak screen, per-user rate and cost budget (Ch51).
Webhook to queue: HMAC signature and webhook-id dedupe. The payload is untrusted data (Ch47, Ch53).
Model proposal to tool: allowlist, then the effect gate. Unknown effects deny. External effects hold (Ch48, Ch29).
Tool and document text to model: wrapped as untrusted data and never placed in the system prompt (Ch9, Ch47).
Approval to side effect: exact tool and args, digest, single-use, 72h, owner match, idempotency key (Ch49).
User to another user's rows: every query filters on userId, including vectors, notes, and the effect ledger (Ch19).
failure_handling: Stop reasons: MODEL_ANSWER, ABSTAIN, STEP_BUDGET, TOKEN_BUDGET, COST_BUDGET, RATE_LIMIT, WAITING_APPROVAL, WAITING_EXPIRED, DENIED, REJECTED, INPUT_BLOCKED, FAILED, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, LOOP_DETECTED (Ch14).
Tool timeout is 15s. Transient job errors retry with backoff. Permanent errors fail the job (Ch14, Ch53).
Side effects use an idempotency key. A lost response is read back from the effect ledger before a second call (Ch53).
Approval timeout expires the row and does not execute. Replay of an approval is rejected (Ch49).
Anthropic 429/5xx falls back to OpenAI once when a key is set. A 400 does not (Ch52).
hitl: Every external effect: the card shows the tool and the full JSON args. The owner approves, edits, or rejects that one call (Ch49).
Edited args are re-hashed and become the exact call. The previous digest cannot be replayed (Ch49).
There is no auto-approve mode in v1. Turning it on would be an explicit risk acceptance, not a default (Ch49).
evals: Golden set evals/golden.json: happy path, chat with no tools, hold, approve, edit, reject, expiry, replay, injection, unknown tool, declared-read override, step budget, loop, abstain, citation, owner isolation, jailbreak, secret redaction, research read-only, coding extension, idempotent note, cost budget, rate limit (Ch42).
Dimensions: task, safety, abstention, efficiency. Safety is zero-tolerance (Ch41, Ch45).
npm test runs the suite. npm run evals prints PROMOTE or HOLD. One safety miss HOLDs the release (Ch45).
risks: Prompt injection in email steering a send: the gate does not read content, and the send still holds. Owner: platform (Ch46, Ch47).
Composio or a remote MCP server is a dependency: the hub isolates them behind one envelope. Owner: founder (Ch59).
Approval rubber-stamping: the card shows the full payload. Audit records the decision. Owner: product (Ch49).
Memory poisoning: a remembered fact cannot change the gate, and retrieval is owner-scoped. Owner: platform (Ch18).
Creating an issue or comment is classified as an internal write. Residual risk, accepted for v1. Owner: founder (Ch46).
non_goals: A React Native client, push notifications, and voice
